articles.title: Joe Burrow is positioned very well to win his first NFL MVP award
articles.summary: Joe Burrow is off to a fantastic start for the Bengals this season.
articles.body:
It has always seemed that at some point, Joe Burrow will win an NFL MVP award.

He has been in the conversation before. In 2024 he might have won had the Cincinnati Bengals simply made the playoffs, but they were not good enough around him.

Burrow is fairly quietly having a season that might be his best in the NFL, and that's saying something. He has 1,653 yards, 15 touchdowns and three interceptions for a team that is now favored to win the AFC North. On the road, in a huge divisional game against the Baltimore Ravens last week, Burrow threw for 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half as the Bengals came back to win 35-13. That bumped up Burrow's MVP odds in the betting market. BetMGM has him second behind Josh Allen, who has +140 odds (bet $100 to win $140). Burrow is second at +450. That gap should shrink in upcoming weeks.

With the Bengals' soft upcoming schedule, it is very easy to envision Burrow leading the race by the end of November. And him not having an MVP award will probably work in his favor.

Burrow has a chance to put up some ridiculous numbers in November. Here is Cincinnati's upcoming schedule with the opposing defense's rank in DVOA : vs. Titans (32nd), at Falcons (11th), vs. Steelers (7th), at Commanders (23rd), vs. Saints (30th).

That's three great matchups and the Falcons and Steelers aren't as scary as their rankings would indicate. Burrow already threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns at Pittsburgh in Week 3. He could pile up some numbers because he's already one of the hottest quarterbacks in the NFL.

Burrow leads the NFL with a completion percentage of 71.7%. His passer rating of 110.4 would be a career best, and is second to only Jared Goff among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. The Bengals are doing a good job protecting him; his sack percentage of 4.4% is by far the best of his career. That number has never been under 6% during Burrow's NFL career. That can keep Burrow healthy, and when he plays behind a competent offensive line he's going to have some huge games.

Of course, Burrow isn't the only quarterback in the mix.

Jared Goff has a similar argument to Burrow. He has thrown 14 touchdowns with no interceptions. The Lions would likely need to win the NFC North — Matthew Stafford was the first MVP winner from a wild-card team since 2008 — but he's putting up numbers to have his name in the conversation. Burrow has a similar issue, and the AFC North is deep and tough like the NFC North.

Allen is the favorite, and for good reason. He's a great player and has had some remarkable games already. What's working against Allen was a big reason he won the 2024 MVP: Voters like to spread the award around. They bypassed Lamar Jackson for his third MVP in 2024, even though he was voted All-Pro quarterback, to get Allen his first award. Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL without an MVP and that usually matters even if it's not spoken out loud.

It all lines up for Burrow. He is off to a great start. He has a line that can keep him healthy and throwing from clean pockets. Cincinnati is favored to win its division. He will put up some great numbers in November. And he has the name cache that will make him easy to vote for if it's close with Allen, Jared Goff, Brock Purdy or anyone else.

Burrow won a Heisman Trophy at LSU years ago. He's got a great path to add an NFL MVP award to his case this season.

articles.title: "Children with life-threatening allergies": Brittany Mahomes launches $100,000 food allergy campaign after son's health scare
articles.summary: In 2023, Brittany Mahomes found a way to turn one of the scariest moments of her family's life into an effort to protect other children.
articles.body: In 2023, Brittany Mahomes found a way to turn one of the scariest moments of her family's life into an effort to protect other children. After her youngest son, Bronze, suffered a frightening allergic reaction to peanuts, the Kansas City Current co-owner decided to support families facing similar challenges. Her personal experience became the driving force behind a fundraising partnership with plant-based nutrition brand OWYN, aimed at supporting food allergy research and helping families deal with potentially life-threatening reactions.Brittany Mahomes' son's peanut allergy scare inspired the donationThe incident happened in August 2023, when Bronze was just eight months old. What began as an ordinary day quickly turned into a medical emergency after the infant experienced an allergic reaction to peanuts. Brittany later shared details of the family's rushed trip to the emergency room on Instagram, describing the experience as “scary and frantic.”For the Mahomes family, the incident was a reminder of how quickly a child's health can become a serious concern. Brittany also called the experience “terrifying,” highlighting the fear parents can face when their children encounter unexpected food allergies.Rather than keeping the experience private, she used it to support an organisation working to make life safer for affected families.On Thursday, December 7, 2023, Brittany and OWYN announced a donation-matching campaign benefiting Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE). The organisation is recognised as the largest private funder of food allergy research in the United States.“I am proud to partner with OWYN on this match donation to FARE. This is a cause that is near and dear to my heart given the support that the nonprofit provides to families like ours who have children with life-threatening food allergies,” Mahomes said.OWYN and Brittany Mahomes launch $100,000 FARE campaignThe fundraising partnership formed part of FARE's biggest annual fundraising initiative. Brittany and OWYN pledged to match donations up to $100,000, giving supporters an opportunity to double the impact of their contributions.The campaign also highlighted the challenges faced by households dealing with severe food allergies and sensitivities. OWYN said it wanted to bring greater attention to the issue and encourage more people to support research and affected families.“We are committed to standing with roughly one-third of U.S. households dealing with a severe food allergy or sensitivity, and we’re calling on you to join us,” Mark Olivieri, CEO of OWYN, said. “This medical condition is an undeniable challenge within our food system, and we’re continuing our dedication to tackling it head on with our donation to FARE.”OWYN also became the first brand to receive national recognition from FARE.Donations were accepted through FoodAllergy.org/MahomesOWYN until December 31, 2023. For Brittany, the initiative offered a meaningful way to turn a frightening family experience into support for parents navigating similar fears.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams": Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes share heartwarming moment with young Chiefs fan after her two open-heart surgeries
articles.summary: For Myka Eilers, meeting Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce was about much more than getting close to her favorite Kansas City Chiefs stars.
articles.body: For Myka Eilers, meeting Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce was about much more than getting close to her favorite Kansas City Chiefs stars. The young football fan had spent much of her early life dealing with a serious heart condition. In May 2022, however, she got a day she had always dreamed of when the Chiefs welcomed her to Arrowhead Stadium through the Make-A-Wish Foundation.What followed was a memorable afternoon filled with football, jokes and a few surprises. Mahomes and Kelce took time to play with Myka, who had her own ambitions of reaching the NFL one day. Her mother, Angela Eilers, later struggled to find words for what the experience meant to their family. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce give Myka Eilers a day she will never forgetMyka's journey had not been easy. She was diagnosed with pulmonary valve stenosis as a newborn, a condition that affects blood flow from the heart to the lungs. She underwent two open-heart surgeries as an infant. Doctors also warned that she might need another procedure in the future.Still, Myka refused to let her condition define her childhood. She played soccer, softball and football, eventually becoming the quarterback of her flag football team. She also had a big ambition: becoming the first woman to play in the NFL.Her love for the Chiefs led her to make a special wish through Make-A-Wish. She initially wanted to go on a Disney cruise, but the pandemic delayed those plans. She then changed her wish and asked to meet Mahomes.The surprise arrived in 2022 when KC Wolf, the Chiefs' mascot, showed up at the Eilers family's home in Yorba Linda, California, with an invitation to Kansas City.On May 25, 2022, Myka and her family arrived at Arrowhead Stadium. During the visit, she found a personalized Chiefs jersey with her name and Mahomes' No. 15 in the quarterback's locker.The biggest surprise came when she stepped onto the field and met Mahomes and Kelce. Mahomes welcomed her with a fist bump before joking about his place on the team."Don't take my spot, though," the quarterback told Myka as she prepared to throw a pass to Kelce. He added, "You can't throw it too good, you know."Myka took her shot anyway. She delivered a pass straight to Kelce, who encouraged her with a playful, "Downtown, Charlie Brown. We're going deep, alright?"The Chiefs tight end then joined her for more football, turning the meeting into something far more personal than a quick photograph with two NFL stars. Myka's mother shares emotional reaction to Chiefs stars' surpriseThe visit also gave Myka a chance to spend time with Mahomes away from the field. She watched game footage with him, including the quarterback's game-winning touchdown pass to Kelce against the Buffalo Bills in the 2021 AFC Divisional Round.She even signed a one-day contract with the Kansas City Chiefs alongside general manager Brett Veach. It was another special touch for a young fan who had dreamed of being part of the team.Angela later recalled the meeting in an interview with TODAY.com, describing Kelce as "a jokester and a fun guy."She also spoke about what the entire experience meant to her daughter and the family. Speaking to Make-A-Wish, Angela said, "Today has been amazing. It's made her feel so special. Our family just feels welcome and seen. We couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams."Myka also remembered the players warmly, telling TODAY.com that Mahomes and Kelce were "really nice and funny; just good people."For a young girl who had faced two open-heart surgeries before she could even understand the game she loved, the day offered something she could carry with her long after leaving Arrowhead Stadium. Mahomes and Kelce did more than meet a young Chiefs supporter. They gave her the chance to step onto the field, throw passes with her heroes and feel like part of the team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "They put a bird's eye view of where we live": Kylie Kelce has a blunt response for critics questioning her family's decision to own multiple neighboring homes
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce had little patience for strangers questioning why her family owns several neighboring properties.
articles.body: Kylie Kelce had little patience for strangers questioning why her family owns several neighboring properties. The wife of former Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce recently explained that the decision has less to do with owning more real estate and more to do with protecting her family. During an October 29 episode of her Not Gonna Lie podcast, Kylie recalled confronting an Instagram account that shared an aerial view of their home. What followed was a heated exchange about security, privacy and the limits of public curiosity.Kylie Kelce explains why her family bought neighboring homesThe issue came up while Kylie was speaking with comedian Nikki Glaser about the kind of criticism public figures face online. She recalled seeing a post from the Instagram account Celeb Homes, which had shared an aerial photograph of the property she shares with Jason and their four daughters.The post went beyond showing the family's home. According to Kylie, it also included details about the property and its surroundings. That did not sit well with her, particularly because the post offered strangers a closer look at where her children live."They put a bird's eye view of where we live with our children, and they were trying to give details of our property," she explained.The discussion became more frustrating when people began questioning why the family had purchased another house next door. Rather than ignore the comments, Kylie decided to make her reason clear."They were like, 'why would you need this many houses?' And I'm like, 'for [expletive] security and privacy, you pieces of [expletive],'" Kylie recalled.For the Kelces, the neighboring properties serve a purpose beyond adding to their real estate holdings. Having control over the surrounding space gives the family more privacy and security, especially with four young children growing up in a household that attracts considerable public attention.Jason and Kylie married in 2018 and are parents to Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finnley. Their family life has become a subject of public interest, but that does not mean Kylie is comfortable with strangers examining the details of their home.Kylie Kelce admits she couldn't resist responding to criticsKylie also revealed that she did not limit her reaction to discussing the incident on her podcast. She went directly to the Instagram post and left a comment explaining why the family wanted the neighboring properties."Why would anyone need three neighboring properties? For safety, privacy, and security. Get the f outta here," she wrote.She had apparently intended to make her response even stronger, but Instagram's content restrictions got in the way."I think I typed 'get [expletive].' And then when I tried to post it, it wouldn't let me," she joked. "Why? I want to tell people to get [expletive]."Her exchange with Glaser offered another glimpse of Kylie's approach to online criticism. She is generally comfortable sharing parts of her life with an audience, but there is a clear difference between public attention and strangers trying to establish details about her children's home.The Kelces' fame may make their property an interesting subject for social media accounts, but Kylie is drawing a line between curiosity and personal security. She was not interested in defending how many houses her family owns. She wanted people to understand why keeping their surroundings private matters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cowboys Get Bad Injury News on $53 Million Cardinals’ 1st-Round Pick
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys get bad injury news on Arizona Cardinals' $50 million 1st-round pick. The post Cowboys Get Bad Injury News on $53 Million Cardinals’ 1st-Round...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' defense doesn't really need more challenges right now — they just need to keep their heads above water.

With every game critical from here on out because of their 3-4 record, the Cowboys now face an unexpected Week 8 challenge from a surprisingly feisty Arizona Cardinals squad, thanks to the return of Arizona's 1st-round pick and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love.

"Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love will play Sunday vs. the Cowboys," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Friday.

"Jeremiyah Love a third straight practice and deemed go to go against Cowboys by Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur," Cardinals reporter Bo Brack wrote on his official X account.

Love has missed the last two games with an ankle injury.

"The rest was needed," Love said on Friday . "It helped me get back to myself … I ain't myself if I ain't got my ankles."

Cardinals Shocked NFL Picking Love at No. 3 Overall

The Cardinals shocked the NFL by selecting Love at No. 3 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft and signing him to a 4-year, $53.02 million contract—fully guaranteed and automatically making him the highest-paid running back in NFL history in total contract value.
